newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Act NZ backs Peters' compulsory pension scheme.
newsitem.headline: Act NZ backs Peters' compulsory pension scheme.

text.p: Act New Zealand on Tuesday backed Treasurer Winston Peters' controversial compulsory superannuation scheme and said it would campaign for a "yes" vote in the September referendum.
However, Act leader Richard Prebble said the referendum was a choice between two imperfect systems and the proposed Retirement Savings Scheme (RSS) had "flaws".
Prebble said Act realised that if it opposed the referendum, "then it is lost".
"While we regard New Zealand First as an unprincipled populist party with an erratic leader, this issue is too important to play politics," he said.
Prebble said there should be full compensatory tax cuts for super contributions and that the scheme should be voluntary.

"There is no actuarial reason why the savings scheme needs to be compulsory, because those taxpayers who elect to remain in the tax-based scheme would continue to pay the higher rate of tax," he said.
Prebble told reporters Act had sought advice from leading actuary John Eriksen, who had advised that New Zealand Superannuation was unsustainable.
Prebble said Act would campaign for a yes vote because of this. Act believed it was vital New Zealand shifted to a savings-based superannuation scheme.
